question.problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=x\,i+(x+y)\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
question.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t, \\ Q(x,y) & =x+y=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the substitution $\operatorname{sin}⁡t=u,du=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }15{cos}^{2}⁡t+9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+15{sin}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }15\,\text{d}t+9{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }15\,\text{d}t+9{\int }_{0}^{0}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =15t{|}_{0}^{2\pi }+0 \\  & =15(2\pi -0) \\  & =30\pi \end{aligned}
$$
